reason: Under the EKS Hybrid Nodes overview page, the quote says the networking is flexible to your preferred method of connecting on-premises networks to a VPC, with documented options Site-to-Site VPN, Direct Connect or your own VPN.
First quote: Karpenter is open-source software customers install, configure and manage; second quote: there is no AWS SLA for Karpenter.
Quotes define extended clusters (control plane in Region, nodes on Outpost) and local clusters (both on Outpost), and state the control plane is fully managed by AWS for both options.
Quote states all EKS clusters have a per cluster per hour fee based on the cluster's Kubernetes version.
Quote on the EKS pricing page states each Provisioned Control Plane scaling tier offers specific capacity and you pay an hourly rate for the tier with no upfront fees or long-term commitments.
Quote on the EKS pricing page lists EC2 instances, EBS volumes, public IPv4 addresses and cross-AZ traffic to the control plane as resources you also pay for.

The quote supports the integration and the EC2 and Fargate wording, but the page marks the feature as applying to Linux nodes with EC2 instances and to private subnets; the claim drops these conditions.
First quote: nodes run in your account, connect via the API server endpoint, billed at EC2 prices; second quote: all instances in a node group must use the EKS node IAM role.
Quote states a stateless application does not save session data and that this makes it easier to replace unhealthy Pods or move them without saving state.
Quote states Amazon EKS is committed to offering support for at least three Kubernetes versions at any given time.
Quote carries the 7-day rollback window after an in-place upgrade, the EXTENDED upgrade policy requirement and the auto-upgrade exception.
Quote states VPA automatically adjusts CPU and memory reservations to right size applications, which can improve cluster resource utilization.
Quote states Fargate tasks require awsvpc, which gives each task an ENI, and that you must specify one or more subnets and one or more security groups.
Quote states Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2 usage regardless of family, size, Region, OS or tenancy and also apply to Fargate and Lambda usage.
Quote on the EKS Fargate Pod page states each Pod receives a default 20 GiB of ephemeral storage that is deleted after the Pod stops.
Table row under the vCPU/memory header on the EKS Fargate Pod page: 16 vCPU, between 32 GB and 120 GB in 8-GB increments.
Quote states 20 GiB ephemeral storage per workload, erased after it stops, expandable up to 200GiB on ECS and 175 GiB on EKS.
Quote states each ECS task or Pod gets a dedicated ENI carrying all traffic, secured by security groups and network ACLs and monitored with Flow Logs.
Decision guide quote states the 15-minute maximum execution time per invocation and the listed well-suited scenarios.
Quota row gives 25 for the listed Regions, 100 for each other Region, Adjustable Yes, and the note of 25 for Regions introduced after May 20, 2025, for on-demand ECS tasks or EKS pods per burst.
Quota row gives 5 per second for the listed Regions, 20 for each other Region, Adjustable Yes, and the note of 5 for Regions introduced after May 20, 2025.
Quotes state per-second pricing with a 1-minute minimum, the duration from image pull to termination rounded up, and a 5-minute minimum for Windows containers.
Quote states a private-subnet Fargate task needs a NAT gateway to pull images, and with ECR an interface VPC endpoint lets the pull use the task's private IPv4 address.
Quotes state that as of 12/18/2025 ECS lets you configure EC2 event windows for Fargate tasks and that an event window takes precedence over the retirement wait time.
Quotes list ALB, NLB and GWLB for ECS services on Fargate, their layer 7 and layer 4 roles, and the platform version 1.4 or later condition for NLB UDP.
Quote states ECS tasks on Fargate with Linux platform version 1.4.0 can use SOCI to start faster, with a few seconds of image pull while the image downloads in the background, called lazy loading.
Quota row gives 25 Spot ECS tasks per burst for the listed Regions, 100 for each other Region, Adjustable Yes, and the note for Regions introduced after May 20, 2025.
Quote states Spot capacity may be unavailable at high demand, services retry until capacity is available, and Fargate does not replace Spot with on-demand capacity.
Quote states the service scheduler receives the interruption signal and tries to launch more Fargate Spot tasks if capacity exists, and a one-task service is interrupted until capacity is available.
Quota row gives 5 Spot ECS tasks per second for the listed Regions, 20 for each other Region, Adjustable Yes, and the note for Regions introduced after May 20, 2025.
Quote states the two-minute warning at a Spot interruption is sent as a task state change event to EventBridge and as SIGTERM to the running task.
Four quotes carry the route-to-internet requirement, the public IP option for public subnets, the NAT gateway option for private subnets, and the ECR interface endpoint pull over private IPv4.
Table row under the CPU/memory/OS header: 32768 (32 vCPU), requires Linux platform 1.4.0 or later, 60 GB, 120 GB, 244 GB, Linux.

First quote supports task-level CPU and memory with no overhead; but the 'them' of the second quote refers to 'the resource limits' in the preceding sentence, which stands only in the surrounding text, so the quotes alone do not show what is set to the sum of reservations.
Table row under the CPU/memory/OS header: 256 (.25 vCPU), 512 MiB, 1 GB, 2 GB, Linux.
